questions.problem:
$$
{{[\begin{aligned}2 & 3 & -1 \\ 6 & 4 & 1 \\ 4 & 6 & -4\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{A}={{[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 3 & 1 & 0 \\ 2 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{L}\cdot {{[\begin{aligned}2 & 3 & -1 \\ \boxed{} & \boxed{} & \boxed{} \\ 0 & 0 & -2\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{U}.
$$

Consider the LU factorization of the matrix $A$ above. From left to right, what are the missing elements from the second row of the matrix $U?$
questions.worked_solution:
The matrix $U$ in the LU decomposition is obtained from the original matrix $A$ by row-reducing using Gaussian elementation. In particular, to make $0$ at the position ${a}_{21}$ of the matrix $A,$ we proceed as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =[\begin{aligned}2 & 3 & -1 \\ 6 & 4 & 1 \\ 4 & 6 & -4\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-3){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}2 & 3 & -1 \\ 0 & -5 & 4 \\ 4 & 6 & -4\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, from left to right, the elements from the second row of $U$ are $0,-5,$ and $4.$

$$

Consider the LU factorization of the matrix $A$ above. What is the value of the entry ${l}_{32}$ in the matrix $L?$
questions.worked_solution:
The matrix $U$ in the LU decomposition is obtained from the original matrix $A$ by row-reducing using Gaussian elementation. In particular, to make zeros below the main diagonal, we proceed as follows:

$$

$$

Now, we want to make $0$ at the position ${a}_{32}$ using Gaussian elimination. To do this, we take the $3$rd row of $A,$ and we add the $2$nd row of $A$ multiplied by $-4:$

$$
\begin{aligned} & \,\,[\begin{aligned}4 & 0 & 3 \\ 0 & -8 & 5 \\ 0 & -32 & 19\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+(-4){R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}4 & 0 & 3 \\ 0 & -8 & 5 \\ 0 & 0 & -1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

$$
{l}_{32}=-(-4)=4.

questions.knowledge_point: Finding the LU Factorization of a 3x3 Matrix
questions.problem:
$$
D=[\begin{aligned}3 & 4 & 5 \\ -9 & -6 & -6 \\ -3 & -2 & -2\end{aligned}]
$$

If $D=LU$ is the LU decomposition of the matrix $D$ given above, what is the value of ${l}_{32}\cdot {u}_{23}?$
questions.worked_solution:
Let's apply our standard LU factorization algorithm.

We reduce the matrix $D$ to row echelon form to obtain the matrix $U,$ as usual. However, instead of writing zeros below the main diagonal, we will instead write down the entries of the matrix $L.$

$$
\begin{aligned}D & =[\begin{aligned}3 & 4 & 5 \\ -9 & -6 & -6 \\ -3 & -2 & -2\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+3{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}3 & 4 & 5 \\ -3 & 6 & 9 \\ -3 & -2 & -2\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+1{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}3 & 4 & 5 \\ -3 & 6 & 9 \\ -1 & 2 & 3\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+(-\frac{1}{3}){R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}3 & 4 & 5 \\ -3 & 6 & 9 \\ -1 & \,\frac{1}{3}\, & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we obtain

$$
L=[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ -3 & 1 & 0 \\ -1 & \frac{1}{3} & 1\end{aligned}],\,U=[\begin{aligned}3 & 4 & 5 \\ 0 & 6 & 9 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}].
$$

Finally, since ${l}_{32}=\frac{1}{3}$ and ${u}_{23}=9,$ we get

$$
{l}_{32}\cdot {u}_{23}=\frac{1}{3}\cdot 9=3.
$$

If $C=LU$ is the LU decomposition of the matrix $C$ given above, what is the value of ${l}_{41}\cdot {u}_{33}?$
questions.worked_solution:
Let's apply our standard LU factorization algorithm.

We reduce the matrix $C$ to row echelon form to obtain the matrix $U,$ as usual. However, instead of writing zeros below the main diagonal, we will instead write down the entries of the matrix $L.$

$$
\begin{aligned}C & =[\begin{aligned}1 & -3 & 5 & 0 \\ 0 & 8 & -10 & -3 \\ -8 & -8 & 11 & 11 \\ -2 & 6 & -10 & -3\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+8{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -3 & 5 & 0 \\ 0 & 8 & -10 & -3 \\ -8 & -32 & 51 & 11 \\ -2 & 6 & -10 & -3\end{aligned}] & {R}_{4} & :={R}_{4}+2{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -3 & 5 & 0 \\ 0 & 8 & -10 & -3 \\ -8 & -32 & 51 & 11 \\ -2 & 0 & 0 & -3\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+4{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -3 & 5 & 0 \\ 0 & 8 & -10 & -3 \\ -8 & -4 & 11 & -1 \\ -2 & 0 & 0 & -3\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we obtain

$$
L=[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & 0 \\ -8 & -4 & 1 & 0 \\ -2 & 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}],\,U=[\begin{aligned}1 & -3 & 5 & 0 \\ 0 & 8 & -10 & -3 \\ 0 & 0 & 11 & -1 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & -3\end{aligned}].
$$

Finally, since ${l}_{41}=-2$ and ${u}_{33}=11,$ we get

$$
{l}_{41}\cdot {u}_{33}=(-2)\cdot 11=-22.
$$

Consider the LU factorization of the matrix $A$ above. What is the value of $u_{33}$ in the matrix $U?$
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
The matrix $U$ in the LU decomposition is obtained from the original matrix $A$ by row-reducing using Gaussian elementation. In particular, to make zeros below the main diagonal, we proceed as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =[\begin{aligned}1 & -5 & 6 \\ 4 & -9 & 8 \\ 6 & -8 & 10\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-4){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -5 & 6 \\ 0 & 11 & -16 \\ 6 & -8 & 10\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+(-6){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -5 & 6 \\ 0 & 11 & -16 \\ 0 & 22 & -26\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+(-2){R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -5 & 6 \\ 0 & 11 & -16 \\ 0 & 0 & 6\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $u_{33}=6.$

canonical_examples.worked_solution:
We want to make $0$ at the position $a_{{\color{blue}3}{\color{red}1}}$ using Gaussian elimination. To do this, we take the ${\color{blue}3}$rd row of $A,$ and we add the ${\color{red}1}$st row of $A$ multiplied by ${\color{purple}-4}{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & -3 \\ 2 & -6 & 1 \\ 4 & 8 & -10\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+(-4){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & -3 \\ 2 & -6 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 2\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The entry $l_{{\color{blue}3}{\color{red}1}}$ of the matrix $L$ is the factor next to $R_1,$ taken with the opposite sign:

$$
l_{31}=-({\color{purple}-4})=4
$$
